title: openalex_W4413925067
universal_lens: A 3D task space reconstruction from partial views enables 2D diffusion planning with inverse warping to constrain motion in real-world robotic navigation. A 2D motion of interest (MOI) conditioned on 3D environmental motion (Env-M) enables knowledge transfer through task-space control and trajectory reconstruction.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief updates over 2D image-space plans conditioned on 3D task constraints via conformal predictive distributions. Bayesian inference maps expert trajectories to policy parameters via probabilistic conditioning on observed ball and wheelchair motion in task space.
gse_mapping: Situationally aware state transitions in 2D image space enable dynamic planning loops with PD control feedback for real-time wheelchair tennis navigation. Situationally grounded state transitions model the evolution of wheelchair motion relative to ball dynamics using conformal predictive distributions.

primitives.name: Diffusion Motion Planning
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our pipeline enables diffusion-based imitation learning by reconstructing the full 3D task space from multiple partial views, warping it into 2D image space, closing the planning loop within this 2D space, and transfer constrained motion of interest back to task space.

primitives.assumptions: Partial views are sufficient to reconstruct 3D structure; 2D warping preserves topological integrity of motion paths.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When 3D view occlusion exceeds 50%, reconstruction accuracy degrades below 90%.

layer2.mapping: The 3D-to-2D warp maps a geometrically constrained planning domain to an image-based policy space, enabling diffusion-based imitation learning.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces a novel framework for zero-shot knowledge transfer in robotic sports navigation, specifically wheelchair tennis, leveraging web videos of expert performance. The core innovation lies in a diffusion-based imitation learning pipeline that reconstructs a full 3D task space from partial views, warps it into 2D image space for planning, and transfers constrained motion back to 3D task space. This approach addresses the scarcity of expert demonstrations in agile robotics by utilizing readily available broadcast videos. The method combines domain knowledge transfer with adversarial constraints to ensure robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios. The framework's ability to generalize to other 2D mobile robot navigation problems underscores its theoretical and practical significance. The integration of a local planner with position control enables real-time feedback planning, crucial for dynamic environments such as tennis courts. The empirical validation shows high success rates in both simulation and real-world experiments, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in bridging the gap between perception, planning, and control in robotic sports.
